sections.content: You know *más*/*menos*... *que* and *tan*... *como* from A2 Unit 6. New here are the superlatives. The relative superlative uses *el/la/los/las más/menos* + adjective (+ *de*), and *mejor*/*peor* become *el/la mejor*, *el/la peor*. The absolute superlative says “very” with *-ísimo/-ísima*: *útil* becomes *utilísimo*.

items.spanish: La práctica es más eficaz que memorizar listas.
items.english: Practice is more effective than memorising lists.

items.spanish: Esta es la estrategia más eficaz de todas.
items.english: This is the most effective strategy of all.

items.spanish: Para mí, practicar con otras personas es la mejor opción.
items.english: For me, practising with other people is the best option.

items.spanish: Este método es utilísimo para aprender vocabulario.
items.english: This method is extremely useful for learning vocabulary.

sections.content: Use *el/la más* + adjective for the relative superlative, *el/la mejor* and *el/la peor* for good and bad, and *-ísimo* for “very”. Never say *más mejor*.
